observations.statement: The testing runtime defines distinct receipt-backed records for method research, method selection, installation, harness probing, test strategy, visible sessions, test-run results, policy overrides, and cleanup.
Method research must cite at least one official source, and stale research blocks Auto selection; selection must choose a listed candidate and cannot select under Off policy.
Installation records exact tool/version/command/change/log/rollback facts, require authority for global or privileged installation, and require rollback or cleanup to be recorded.
A passing harness probe requires evidence, a blocked probe records a gap, a completed strategy requires generated or reused tests, and strategy gaps must become blockers or approved exceptions.
Visible-session and test-run pass claims require evidence; visible sessions additionally require interaction events and redaction, while manual-only work cannot certify an automated pass.
Testing overrides carry scope, capability, risk, approval, evidence, redaction, reopening or expiration, and truthful-result data; they cannot produce test_passed or full certification.

Auto, On, and Off have distinct testing-selection behavior: Auto is authority-bounded, On blocks when unavailable or unauthorized, and Off neither uses nor installs and requires an override for affected certification scope.
Cleanup is receipt-backed; temporary installs require cleanup or approved retention, cleanup failure blocks, and cleanup is intended to link attempts to final certification.

The UI command section represents actions and navigation wrappers through named payload/result fields, guards, disabled reasons, receipt effects, stale-projection policy, idempotency fields, and recovery routes.

Source import is gated by current workspace, permission, security policy, and a resource-limit profile; it returns security/resource/intake receipts and offers retry, removal, quarantine, and authority-request recovery.
Source annotation requires a current or relocated anchor and an authorized actor, preserves original selected text, and remaps or blocks a stale anchor before applying the action.
Planning commands cover starting from an approved PRD, topic creation and mutation, impact/defer/reopen operations, amendment acceptance, and approval into a build.

approve_and_build carries revisions and hashes across the planning run, topic map, plan pack, project context, PlanUnit index, acceptance index, testing policy, and final audit closure; it synchronously creates or binds one PlanCompileRun under a final-review CAS.

Compile controls expose pause, resume, cancel, stage retry, bounded recompile, and evidence/blocker/assignment navigation; open_build is gated on active activation plus BuildStarted existence and waits for a durable BuildStarted projection.
The clean-room harness names an eight-state approval-to-BuildStarted sequence.
Positive scenarios cover duplicate PlanApproved delivery, greenfield, FileSafe, remote SSH, GUI-visible testing, and activation restart.
Negative scenarios require schema rejection for invalid quality, missing visible-session evidence, empty completed worklists, and incomplete terminal compile waves, among other listed cases.
The harness explicitly treats scenarios as static fixtures and schema validation/presence as preconditions; runtime lifecycle certification requires executable evidence.
The core excludes two retired chain-wizard paths from search.

Context, not used to substantiate a core finding, says activation resumes idempotently after restart, duplicate activation keys return an existing GoalRun, requests are accepted atomically, and BuildStarted is delivered exactly once.

candidate_findings.title: Named fields are not executable type contracts
candidate_findings.statement: Within this window, payload_contract and result_contract are arrays of field names but provide no field types, required-versus-optional rules, nullability, formats, bounds, enum domains, cross-field validation, or structured validation-error result.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent UI and runtime builders can accept different payloads, serialize different results, and report incompatible failures while each appears to implement the named contract.

candidate_findings.title: Guard and disabled-reason coverage is internally incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: Several commands do not provide a disabled reason corresponding to each declared guard, and some reason codes refer to conditions not present in the guards: resolve_conflict has ledger_writable but only missing_claims; rename_topic has topic_exists but only duplicate_title; mark_impacted guards topic_map_current but reports missing_impact_evidence; open_build has build_started_exists but no missing-BuildStarted reason.
candidate_findings.impact: The GUI and command dispatcher cannot deterministically map every failed guard to a stable reason, so enablement, accessibility announcements, telemetry, and recovery routing can diverge.

candidate_findings.title: Idempotency-key derivation is underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: Multiple idempotency_key_fields are absent from their payloads, including source_hashes, pack_hash, pack_id, pack_version, project_context_hash, merge_hash, impact_hash, and project_id; arrays such as topic_ids also lack canonical ordering and hash canonicalization rules.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent retries can compute different keys, distinct requests can alias, and clients can disagree about whether an existing result must be returned, risking duplicate mutations or lost operations.

candidate_findings.title: Mutation authorization is not uniformly contracted
candidate_findings.statement: Import and annotation expose permission or actor-authorization guards, and amendment acceptance carries an approver, but the planning-topic mutations and compile pause/resume/cancel/retry contracts shown here carry no actor, authority reference, or authorization guard.
candidate_findings.impact: Authorization ownership and audit attribution for consequential mutations are left to builders, allowing inconsistent enforcement across entry points.

candidate_findings.title: Testing records lack a lifecycle and ordering contract
candidate_findings.statement: The testing runtime lists records and local invariants but does not define an initial state, transitions, required ordering between research, selection, installation, probing, strategy, execution, visible evidence and cleanup, or terminal/cancelled/retry states.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders must invent when records become authoritative, which failures short-circuit certification, whether retries supersede prior evidence, and when cleanup is mandatory, producing incompatible certification behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Research freshness computation is undefined
candidate_findings.statement: method_research supplies retrieved_at_utc and freshness_ttl and says stale research blocks Auto, but the window does not define the TTL unit and boundary, clock source/skew handling, version-change invalidation, refresh behavior, or the failure result when refresh cannot complete.
candidate_findings.impact: The same research can be considered fresh by one implementation and stale by another, changing test-method selection and whether work blocks.

candidate_findings.title: Cleanup linkage cannot be validated from its required fields
candidate_findings.statement: cleanup_rules require cleanup receipts to link to WorkNode attempts and final certification, but cleanup_receipt required_fields contain no WorkNode-attempt reference or final-certification reference.
candidate_findings.impact: A cleanup record can satisfy its declared required fields while failing the stated traceability obligation, preventing reliable closure and certification linkage.

candidate_findings.title: Redaction evidence and disposition are not represented consistently
candidate_findings.statement: visible_session requires only redaction_applied, while visible-session rules require redaction evidence and a redaction disposition; the visible_session record has no redaction-evidence, disposition, or profile field even though testing_policy_override separately carries redaction_profile_ref.
candidate_findings.impact: Sensitive-session evidence can be marked passing without a typed, auditable explanation of what was redacted, under which profile, or why redaction was disabled.

candidate_findings.title: Test-run reproducibility metadata is incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: test_run_result records test refs, command, result, evidence, and artifacts but no execution time, environment, platform, tool or harness version, exit status, duration, policy snapshot, attempt identity, or ordering identity.
candidate_findings.impact: A pass receipt may be impossible to reproduce or distinguish from another attempt, weakening evidence provenance and retry adjudication.

candidate_findings.title: Override expiry and approval enforcement are left open
candidate_findings.statement: testing_policy_override stores approver_ref, approved_at_utc, and expiration_or_reopen_condition, but the window defines neither who qualifies as explicit user authority nor how expiration or reopening invalidates an override and downstream certification projections.
candidate_findings.impact: Expired or unauthorized exceptions may continue to affect results, and implementations can disagree on when affected scopes return to blocked.

candidate_findings.title: Compile control races lack revision or CAS semantics
candidate_findings.statement: approve_and_build defines revisions, hashes, final-review CAS comparison, synchronous binding, and stable run identity, but pause, resume, cancel, retry_stage, and bounded recompile carry no observed revision, expected state, sequence number, or CAS token and define no conflict outcome for concurrent controls.
candidate_findings.impact: Racing UI commands can act on stale compile state, invert pause/resume order, retry an obsolete stage, or cancel/recompile after intervening mutation with implementation-dependent outcomes.

candidate_findings.title: Execution failures and partial effects have no command contract
candidate_findings.statement: The command entries specify pre-dispatch disabled reasons and successful receipt effects, but this window does not define runtime error taxonomies, atomicity, rollback, partial-result shape, timeout, cancellation acknowledgement, persistence of failed attempts, or retryability after dispatch.
candidate_findings.impact: A command can pass its guard and then fail with no interoperable rule for state, receipts, user-visible truth, or safe recovery.

candidate_findings.title: Recovery routes are names without callable contracts
candidate_findings.statement: Recovery routes such as resume_compile, pause_compile, preserve_cancelled_state, record_stage_blocker, and clear_recompile_request are listed only as names; their payloads, guards, effects, authority, idempotency, success receipts, and failure behavior are not defined here.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders must invent whether recovery is navigation or mutation and whether it is safe, authorized, repeatable, and auditable.

candidate_findings.title: Harness expected terminal states do not align with the declared state machine
candidate_findings.statement: The state_machine contains eight named states, while positive expected_terminal_state values include prose outcomes such as same PlanCompileRun returned, source-control setup preflight required, FileSafe preflight accepted, remote adapter preflight accepted, visible test session required, and resume to entrypoints_queued; none are exact members of the state list.
candidate_findings.impact: An executable harness has no unambiguous terminal-state enum or mapping, so scenario completion and transition assertions are builder-defined.

candidate_findings.title: Static scenarios lack executable fixture and failure-oracle detail
candidate_findings.statement: Negative scenarios state schema rejected and provide must_prove labels, but this window supplies no fixture payloads, schema/version references, validator entrypoint, expected error code/path, or exact assertion format; the authority rule confirms that the scenarios remain static until an executable harness drives them.
candidate_findings.impact: Scenario presence can pass while no one can deterministically execute or certify the rejection behavior, and builders must invent the evidence oracle.

candidate_findings.title: Scenario-family certification granularity is undefined
candidate_findings.statement: Lifecycle certification requires executable evidence for each positive and negative scenario family, but the window does not define family identifiers, membership, parameterization, coverage thresholds, evidence aggregation, or whether every listed scenario must execute.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can claim certification from different subsets of scenarios and incomparable evidence bundles.

candidate_findings.title: UI accessibility and user-visible failure behavior are absent
candidate_findings.statement: Although the section is named ui_command_contracts, its entries define command mechanics but no accessible names, keyboard behavior, focus restoration, disabled-state announcements, progress/cancellation presentation, destructive-action confirmation, localization, or mapping from reason codes to user-visible copy.
candidate_findings.impact: The command layer cannot serve as a complete GUI contract, and accessibility plus truthful failure presentation will vary by builder.

candidate_findings.title: Log availability is discretionary without evidence
candidate_findings.statement: Visible-session rules require console and network logs only when available, but do not require a capability probe, unavailable reason, or receipt field recording why either log class is absent.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can omit diagnostically important logs while producing indistinguishable passing visible-session receipts.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Research provenance and freshness are not wholly omitted: official source refs are mandatory and stale research explicitly blocks Auto selection.
Method selection constrains candidate membership and explicitly prohibits selection under Off policy.
Privileged/global installation authority, exact installation change evidence, and rollback-or-cleanup recording are explicit.
Evidence-free pass and manual-only automated certification are explicitly prohibited for the relevant test records.
Off or restricted testing cannot silently become a pass: it requires explicit approval, cannot yield test_passed or full certification, and is limited to an approved-exception or blocked label.
GUI-visible testing has an explicit interaction/evidence/redaction obligation and both a positive required-session scenario and a negative no-evidence rejection scenario.
Source import explicitly runs security/resource preflight before projection dispatch and provides quarantine and authority-request recovery.
Stale source annotations do not silently apply: original selected text is preserved and the anchor must be remapped or blocked.

approve_and_build has strong currentness and idempotency coverage through revisions, content hashes, a final-review CAS, synchronous run creation/binding, and a rule that run identity may not reconcile later.
Compile cancellation explicitly disables once mutation is active, and build navigation waits for active activation plus a durable BuildStarted projection.
Duplicate approval delivery, environment variants, GUI-visible testing, and activation restart all have named positive scenarios with stated proof goals.
The certification authority explicitly refuses to equate static scenario presence or schema validation with lifecycle certification and demands executable evidence after runtime enablement.

unknowns.statement: Whether schemas outside this window define types, validation rules, and structured errors for every named payload/result field cannot be determined from the assigned evidence.
The identity source, authority hierarchy, and verification mechanism behind authority, actor_authorized, approver_ref, and explicit user approval are not defined in this window.
Whether a shared command executor elsewhere supplies atomicity, post-dispatch failure receipts, timeout, concurrency, and recovery semantics is unknown from this window.
The actual GUI components, reason-code copy, localization, focus behavior, and accessibility mapping consuming ui_command_contracts are not named here.
The redaction profile schema, redaction evidence shape, treatment of explicitly disabled redaction, and reviewer authority for sensitive evidence are not available in this window.
No executable harness implementation, fixture location, schema identifier, validator command, or evidence-bundle schema is identified in the clean-room block.
Whether expected_terminal_state is intended as an enum member, a free-text outcome, or a state-plus-assertion composite is not stated.
The consumer, enforcement point, and lifecycle effect of retired_search_exclusions are not identified in the assigned core.
The context defines activation idempotency and exactly-once BuildStarted delivery, but the assigned core does not state how those context-level receipts are bound to clean-room scenario evidence.
